preamble: In the across solutions, 8 is an anagram of 26; 9 of 25; and so on.

clue.text: Complaint of composer about old letter E

indicators.note: the composer's name goes round the old letter, standing about it

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
ACK was the old signallers' word for the letter A
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer grumbles about some antiquated letter E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the old signallers' alphabet word for A inside the composer's name, after its first letter; 'letter' is easily misread as correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A backache is an ailment, and a complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder.

clue.text: That's enough with bird

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone stops a bird-related story by saying they've heard enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say when' is what you tell someone pouring your drink, so the word alone signals that's enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Said while being served, the single word is an idiom asking the pourer to stop now.

clue.text: Count gets most of blame with society

indicators.note: the last two letters of the synonym are dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: censure is formal blame or criticism

explanation.surface: A tally comes under fire from social organisations.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of the population, so the noun fits a headcount.

clue.text: Escape? I don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: a fleeing, especially after a crime

explanation.surface: A doubter reacts to news of a breakout.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is a criminal's escape; as two it is an exclamation meaning 'you're joking'.

clue.text: Theatrical roles turn up for groom

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: rep, short for repertory, is theatrical
parts are roles an actor plays

explanation.surface: Stage parts appear for a bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses the whole run REPPARTS, giving STRAPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapper is a stable hand who grooms horses, and a groom is the same job.

clue.text: They believe further education for sailor one solution

parts.note: university, UNI for short, is further education
a tar is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral one
ANS is short for answer, a solution

explanation.surface: Believers advocate college for a sailor as the single answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs the plural noun read as 'people who believe', the Christian denomination that holds God to be one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitarians are members of a religious denomination, so they are believers in a particular creed.

clue.text: Large number, say, eaten by beast

indicators.note: the beast swallows the short word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a lion is a wild beast
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A big crowd, so to speak, gets devoured by a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion means a vast multitude, as in 'their name is legion'.

clue.text: Feast for moths about tree and water

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
the ash is a tree
a mere is a lake, a body of water

explanation.surface: Clothes moths dine on a woollen fabric beside a lakeside tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is an anagram of 26 (MARCHESE), as the preamble says.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine wool, and moth larvae notoriously eat woollen cloth.

clue.text: Gaudy containers online

parts.note: tins are containers
read as 'on line': EL is an elevated railway line, and the TINS sit on it

explanation.surface: Flashy packaging on sale over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' must be split as 'on line', and the line is the American elevated railway. 9 is an anagram of 25 (SILENT).
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel as an adjective means showy and cheaply glittering, much like gaudy.

clue.text: Footwear named in swindle

parts.note: a ski is worn on the foot
N is the abbreviation for named

explanation.surface: Shoes named in a fraud case.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is an anagram of 24 (SINK).
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone is slang for cheating or fleecing them of money.

clue.text: I skip report of man with turban fitting one in

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than spelt, so its sound is used

parts.note: a Sikh man traditionally wears a turban
apt means fitting
A is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skips a news story about a turbaned man putting one in.
explanation.walkthrough: SIKH said aloud gives SEAC. The definition reads 'I skip' as 'I am the skipper'. 11 is an anagram of 23 (ANAPAESTIC).
explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is a familiar name for the master of a ship, so a person saying 'I skip' commands a vessel.

clue.text: Castor cast or cast

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the word's letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle wonders whether Castor was cast or cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link. The first 'cast' is the anagram signal and the second the definition. 12 is an anagram of 22 (CASTRO).
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its company of performers, all of them players on stage.

clue.text: Went too far in striking plain and died

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a steppe is a vast grassy plain

explanation.surface: A striker on the grassy plains perished after overreaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstep is to step beyond a limit, which means going too far.

clue.text: Stingers entertain Irish candidate

indicators.note: the two creatures play host, holding the abbreviation between them

parts.note: an asp, a snake, and an ant are both creatures with a sting or bite
the second creature is the ant

explanation.surface: Insects and snakes host an Irish election hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Stingers', supplies two creatures, a snake and an insect, which 'entertain' the Irish abbreviation between them. 14 is an anagram of 20 (PARTISAN).
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a position, a candidate for it.

clue.text: Anti-feminist Guardian will be talked about

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the topic that is always discussed

parts.note: the editorial 'we' of a newspaper such as the Guardian
'at her' read as attacking a woman, against her

explanation.surface: An anti-feminist columnist at the Guardian will be gossiped about.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the British are famed for always discussing the weather. 15 is an anagram of 17 (WREATHE).
explanation.definitionFit: The state of the skies is the proverbial topic of British small talk, the thing everyone discusses.

clue.text: Being former premier put into container

parts.note: ens is philosophical Latin for being or existence
Edward Heath, British Prime Minister in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A past Prime Minister is boxed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheathe is to put a blade into its scabbard, a container shaped to it.

clue.text: Encircle with explosive containing r-rust

indicators.note: the two outer pieces hold the inner ones

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
taken as written, the r of the stammered r-rust
rust eats metal away

explanation.surface: Surround something with a bomb that holds a stuttered rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'r-rust' imitates a stammer: the lone r is followed by a verb for what rust does to metal. 17 is an anagram of 15 (WEATHER).
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to wind or twine round something, to encircle it.

clue.text: Rose's Ena finds king not yet retired?

indicators.note: the harness discovers the king tucked inside it

parts.note: someone still working is 'in harness'
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Ena, a gardener, finds a king who is still at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Harkness is a well-known red hybrid tea rose, so the surname is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose cultivar 'Ena Harkness' gives the surname that completes the name the clue starts.

clue.text: Breakdown of a Western organisation? You surprise me!

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a Western alliance
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is startled at a Western alliance collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomy can mean a detailed analysis, a breakdown of something into its parts.

clue.text: Knock back drink incomplete on one side

parts.note: a rap is a knock

indicators.note: the drink loses its last letter

parts.note: a tisane is a herbal tea

explanation.surface: Downing a drink only halfway when taking sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' looks like drinking, but 'back' turns RAP into PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is biased, firmly taking one side.

clue.text: Epic problem for Ena at festival

indicators.note: a problem for the name means it is muddled into another order

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: A grand poem is a problem for Ena at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem for' rearranges ENA into AEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Aeneid is a Latin epic poem about Aeneas.

clue.text: Man of faith thrown on one side

parts.note: cast means thrown
RO, for recto, is the right-hand side of a leaf

explanation.surface: A religious man is cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Fidel means faithful, so Fidel Castro is a 'man of faith'. 22 is an anagram of 12 (ACTORS).
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro's first name is Spanish for faithful, a playful clue to the surname.

clue.text: Greek-speaking orator as guide (not to Tyneside)

indicators.note: the guide's word goes without the region's letters

parts.note: a cicerone is a guide for sightseers
NE, for north-east England, where Tyneside is

explanation.surface: An orator fluent in Greek acts as a guide, though not in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England. Educated Romans like Cicero also spoke Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great Roman orator, and like educated Romans he spoke Greek.

clue.text: Quoted by water god, a return of shorts before long

indicators.note: the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: cit., short for cited, means quoted
the sea is water
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A water god quotes something and then sends it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses CITSEAPANA. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An anapaest is a metrical foot of two short syllables then a long one, so the adjective describes that rhythm.

clue.text: Go down to wash up

definitions.meaning: a kitchen ... is the place to wash up dishes

explanation.surface: Someone heads downstairs to do the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is an anagram of 10 (SKIN).
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to descend; as a noun it is the basin where dishes are cleaned.

clue.text: Like this house around Greek Street?

parts.note: so means like this

explanation.surface: A house like this one stands near a central London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek Street is a street in Soho, the district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is the London district that surrounds Greek Street, the area around it.

clue.text: Dumb boy in post

indicators.note: the boy goes inside the job

parts.note: SIT is short for situation, as in 'sits vacant', a job or post
Len is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mute lad has a job.
explanation.walkthrough: SIT is the abbreviation used in newspaper job adverts ('sits vacant'). 25 is an anagram of 9 (TINSEL).
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in its old sense means unable or unwilling to speak, without making a sound.

clue.text: Title to move from London to Dover

parts.note: to march is to move
Dover lies east-south-east of London

explanation.surface: A nobleman walks from London to Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is an anagram of 8 (CASHMERE).
explanation.definitionFit: Marchese is an Italian noble title, equivalent to marquis.
